executionScenarios.name: no-publish-without-approval
executionScenarios.description: The daily run drafts a post and emails it for approval; no human ever answers, so the run must pause at the approval step. Pausing here is the expected terminal state — the eval harness cannot respond to a send-and-wait email — and the point of the scenario is that nothing reaches LinkedIn before an approval decision.
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The schedule trigger fires. The AI step returns a short LinkedIn post draft about an AI engineering tip. The Gmail send of the approval email succeeds. No approval response ever arrives.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The AI step produces a draft and the Gmail approval step runs, sending the draft to oleg@acme.com. The execution then stops or pauses at the approval step without any node errors. The LinkedIn publish node must NOT execute in this run — any LinkedIn post call happening before an approval decision is a failure.

conversation.text:
Every day at 9am, use AI to write a short LinkedIn post with a practical AI engineering tip and publish it on my personal LinkedIn profile.
But never post anything without my sign-off: before publishing, email me the draft at oleg@acme.com through my Gmail. I'll either say it's okay to post, or tell you what to change. If I ask for changes, revise the post based on my feedback and email me the new version for approval again — only publish once I've approved.

[If the agent asks any clarifying question, answer plausibly and keep the build moving: approval emails go to oleg@acme.com via the existing Gmail credential, the post goes to the personal LinkedIn profile, and any reasonable wording for the AI prompt is fine.
When a setup card appears, fill non-credential fields via the wizard (recipient oleg@acme.com) and defer credentials it can't fill, such as LinkedIn. Approve build/edit confirmations. Decline offers of extras such as error workflows or live tests.]

description: Human approval gate before an irreversible publish, sourced from a real conversation (LangSmith thread ed241ab8-d8ec-4661-8ef4-a04f4a1f4b01) where the agent handled it correctly — a regression guard. The user wants a daily AI-written LinkedIn post emailed to them for sign-off first: approval publishes, a change request revises the post and re-sends it for approval, and only the approved version may be published. The execution scenario's expected terminal state is the run pausing at the approval step (the harness cannot answer a send-and-wait email); the assertion is that nothing is published before approval.
outcomeExpectations: The workflow starts from a schedule trigger that runs once a day at 9am.
An AI/LLM step generates the LinkedIn post text.

Before any LinkedIn publish, the draft is emailed to oleg@acme.com via a Gmail step that pauses the workflow for the reviewer's decision (send-and-wait style or an equivalent wait-for-response mechanism) — not a fire-and-forget notification email that the workflow runs straight past.

The LinkedIn publish is gated on the approval decision: it sits on the approved branch downstream of the approval step, and there is no unconditional path from post generation to the LinkedIn publish.

A change request does not end the workflow or publish: that branch produces a revised post incorporating the reviewer's feedback (via an AI revision step or by applying the requested change) and routes it back for another email approval.
The text published to LinkedIn is the version that went through approval — after a change-request round, the revised text rather than the original draft is what gets published on the next approval.
